asks: MLA Wright asks the commission to keep its interim Edmonton-Beverly-Clareview boundaries and to add another seat in Edmonton.

quote: the loss of the riding around Slave Lake and that sort of thing to make the bigger Mackenzie, that’s an incredibly tough decision
note: Answer to Samson's question on whether she read the whole report; calls the interim Lesser Slave Lake decision tough, makes no request.

asks: MLA Sweet accepts the interim Edmonton-Manning boundaries, supports more Edmonton seats given north-side growth, and asks for a different riding name (not Horse Hill).
MLA Long asks that Jasper, Hinton and Grande Cache stay together in West Yellowhead rather than Jasper joining a Banff-Jasper riding.

quote: There are three distinct regions along the mountains: Jasper and Hinton; Banff, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre; and Canmore, Kananaskis.
note: Describes Rocky Mountain House and Sundre as one central mountain region while arguing for Jasper with Hinton; offered as context, not a request about the RMH riding. Narrow code (rule 17).

quote: There are three distinct regions along the mountains: Jasper and Hinton; Banff, Rocky Mountain House, Sundre; and Canmore, Kananaskis.
note: Groups Banff with Rocky Mountain House and Sundre, apart from Canmore, as a natural region; could be read as a direction toward B1/B9, but it is description supporting his Jasper-Hinton request, not a request. Narrow code (rule 17). Main request is CANMORE-JASPER J1 (not coded here).

asks: MLA Lunty asks that Beaumont not be split and suggests that, if kept whole, Beaumont go into a southeast Edmonton riding because Leduc-Beaumont would be too large.
MLA Batten asks to keep the 2017 Calgary-Acadia boundaries (keeping Kingsland and Manchester, not adding Lake Bonavista), moving only Highfield and Bonnybrook to Calgary-Confluence.
MLA Neudorf asks for more MLAs for Lethbridge (three or four) through urban-rural hybrid ridings, and if it stays at two, to keep the existing east-west lines rather than the new draft.

quote: Would you agree with that description? Mr. Neudorf: Yes, I would. I think it is very essential to maintain the seats in rural and urban-rural hybrids across the province
note: Answer 'yes' to the Chair's description of the Mills proposal: 'take Lethbridge and carve it up into four hybrid ridings so we have a band of six ridings across the south'. Earlier (pp. 425-428) he says more representation 'would be beneficial, be that three, be that four' and leaves the design to the commission, so direction not exact. Fallback: 'If we're going to leave it as two, then leave it the way they are' (L1, current lines), noted not coded.

asks: MLA Ceci asks that the Elbow River, not 1st Street S.E., be Calgary-Buffalo's eastern boundary, keeping East Village, Cliff Bungalow, Mission and the Beltline in it, and supports adding Calgary-Confluence.
Continuation of MLA Ceci's appearance: he restates the Elbow River boundary request and says any reduction from Calgary-Buffalo's current 77,000 would be better.
MLA Boparai supports the interim Calgary-Falconridge changes (with north Monterey Park excluded if possible) and asks for a fully urban Calgary seat instead of the Calgary-Okotoks hybrid.

quote: Outside Calgary the Airdrie-Cochrane corridor also gains an additional seat, moving from two to three, with the new AirdrieWest riding in addition to Airdrie-East and Cochrane-Springbank.
note: Cited as evidence that the commission recognized growth; no request about how Airdrie is divided.

quote: Outside Calgary the Airdrie-Cochrane corridor also gains an additional seat, moving from two to three, with the new AirdrieWest riding in addition to Airdrie-East and Cochrane-Springbank.
note: Names Cochrane-Springbank only as part of a seat count; no request.

asks: MLA Arcand-Paul asks to keep Edmonton-West Henday inside Edmonton (ideally keeping Calder and Lewis Estates whole), supports the interim Edmonton-West-Enoch, Banff-Jasper and Mackenzie ridings, and asks for another Edmonton seat.

quote: By creating the riding of Mackenzie, you have proposed to give Indigenous peoples from northern Alberta a distinct voice for the first time in the history of our province.
note: Supports the interim Mackenzie riding (which dissolved Lesser Slave Lake) and answers the push-back: 'history is not always a good reason to keep things the way that they are'. Lesser Slave Lake is not named, so no rejects of K1 is coded (rule 11/17).

quote: in bringing together the three Stoney Nakoda nations along with the Tsuu T’ina Nation and O’Chiese and Sunchild First Nations in Banff-Jasper
note: Praises the interim Banff-Jasper riding for joining the Stoney Nakoda nations with O'Chiese and Sunchild (reserves west of Rocky Mountain House). This is close to B3, but he never names Rocky Mountain House or Clearwater County; narrow code (rule 17). A second reader might code want B3, INTERIM.

asks: MLA Ganley broadly accepts the interim Calgary map, asks for one more Calgary seat, and asks the commission to drop the Calgary-West-Elbow Valley and Calgary-Cross hybrids and use hybrids sparingly.

quote: Airdrie and Okotoks are, I think, actually growing faster than Calgary.
note: Airdrie named only as a fast-growing bedroom city whose residents feel their interests differ from Calgary's; no request about how Airdrie is divided.

asks: MLA Nally asks for more urban-rural hybrid ridings, to keep his St. Albert-Morinville hybrid and add part of Lac Ste. Anne County (with a First Nation) to it, and to keep the name Morinville-St. Albert.

quote: I know that there’s a proposal in front of you to include part of Lac Ste. Anne in Morinville-St. Albert, and I hope you consider that
note: Keeps the long-standing city-county hybrid (consistent with S0) but asks to add part of Lac Ste. Anne County, including Alexander First Nation, to it to offset north St. Albert growth; on no listed option. In answer to Clark's hypothetical he also says 'give Parkland a bigger piece of St. Albert. Then you would get three true St. Albert MLAs' (EB-808, close to S2's three-district feature) and would accept an Edmonton-St. Albert mix 'in addition to, not instead of' the hybrid. Area of Lac Ste. Anne meant is not specified.

asks: MLA Yao asks the commission not to remove a northern constituency and to keep a constituency in the Slave Lake region.

quote: maintaining a constituency in the region of Slave Lake would be a strong symbol of this, in addition to it being logical for other reasons that I mentioned earlier.
note: Rejection: 'My concern today is about the proposed loss of a northern constituency. The proposed constituency lines would result in one less voice' (EB-809).

asks: MLA Al-Guneid supports the interim Calgary-Glenmore boundaries (adding the rest of Lakeview), the added Calgary seat and keeping Calgary ridings within city limits; the record then runs into MLA Hunter's presentation (Coaldale, Lethbridge quad hybrid), which is not coded here.
